key_insight: VLA-Tug proposes a lightweight monitor that probes a vision-language-action model’s internal representations to predict and classify failures. The goal is timely, calibrated warnings without the overhead of a large monitoring system.
problem_solved: Vision-language-action models can fail unpredictably under distribution shift, potentially damaging equipment or endangering people. Real-world deployment needs monitoring that is fast, informative, and efficient enough for edge devices.
method: Attach a lightweight probe to the VLA’s latent layers to monitor internal model signals.
Target calibrated runtime failure prediction and classification. The supplied abstract is truncated, so calibration details and evaluation results are unavailable.
impact: If validated, this approach could help practitioners identify risky robot behavior and make better-informed intervention decisions. Its lightweight design targets deployment on resource-constrained edge hardware.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: camera input and language instruction → VLA → robot action, with a latent probe branching into a failure warning.
Distribution-shift illustration contrasting a familiar workspace with an unexpected obstacle or changed lighting.
Conceptual monitoring dashboard showing failure risk and predicted failure category.
Design-goal icons highlighting timely warnings, calibration, informative outputs, and edge efficiency.
paper_title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
paper_authors: Michal P. Podolinsky, Yunhao Yang, Daniel Little, Hong Lu, Rohan Siva
